_about: The story score: how every Sunday option is scored blind and ordered, as rows (the story engine v5 plan, 26 Nov 2026; docs/proposals/2026-11-26-story-engine-gaps.md). Three stages in a fixed order: the floor (scripts/post-pack/story_floor.py, config/story-floor.json: the only reader of his rejections, pass or refused, never a number), the blind score (scripts/post-pack/story_score.py: anchored 0-10 axes, weighted per content type out of 100, with hard floors per type) and the council on close calls only. Taste is a floor only (Ruling, Krish, 2026-11-26): nothing here reads his picks, his approved taste, why_here, cues, scorecards or his verdicts on formats, and nothing is tuned from his picks automatically. Weights and anchors are a first proposal from the growth evidence below and the rulings; only Krish changes them, by a pull request. A weight, anchor, floor, margin or cost is a row here, never code.
from_note: The first board the Sunday gate holds to the score (codes story and story_floor). 2026-11-30 if this merges before the 29 Nov run; earlier boards keep the order they were made in.

rulings.ruling: His taste is a floor only: his rejections refuse an option, never score it, and the judges stay blind (check-judges.ts section 4, tests/story_wall_test.py).
The blind proof run spends at most $10, through the ledger, after the protocol is committed.
The approved North Star reader line (config/beat.json reader), his words: "I approve the lines".

anchors.10: Changes money, rights or work for a whole sector or for millions of fans and creators, with a sourced figure.
anchors.7: A major named player's move with a measurable second-order effect on others in the sector.
anchors.4: One notable company or creator, with a local consequence.
anchors.1: Trivia, a personnel move or a version bump.

axes.label: Absurd or funny on its own true facts

anchors.10: The plain sourced fact is absurd on its face and the best sound angle reads as supported humour, no explaining needed.
anchors.7: The fact carries a clear incongruity or reversal a stranger gets at once.
anchors.4: A wry detail is there but needs a line of set-up.
anchors.1: Nothing funny in the facts; any joke would cost credibility.

anchors.10: Nobody else is telling it this way, it is specific to this story and the reader can use it today.
anchors.7: A fresh, specific take with one rival telling it nearby.
anchors.4: A familiar take with one specific detail added.
anchors.1: The take every outlet already ran.

axes.label: Holds the five whys
axes.formula: min(10, 2 x documented rungs + 1 x labelled inferred rungs), from scripts/whys-probe-check.ts

anchors.10: Five documented rungs across at least two sites, each quote found verbatim in its page, and an open landing.
anchors.7: Three documented rungs plus labelled inferred ones that reach five, landing open.
anchors.4: Two documented rungs; the ladder stops before the money or the mechanism.

axes.label: On the beat, with its economics

anchors.10: A focus-sector keyword and an economics keyword or money figure in the topic itself.
anchors.7: A focus-sector keyword in the topic.
anchors.4: A focus-sector keyword only in the body.
anchors.1: No focus-sector keyword anywhere (the avoid list is the floor's, not a score).

anchors.10: The hook names a concrete product, work, deal or person, plus a number or a twist.
anchors.7: Named and concrete, with a number or twist in the body only.
anchors.4: Named, but no number and no twist.
anchors.1: Abstract framing with nothing named (the losing pattern in growth_evidence).

anchors.10: A stranger would send it to a friend before finishing it.
anchors.7: Holds a busy reader to the end, with one moment worth repeating.
anchors.4: Useful but flat; read once and forgotten.

anchors.10: A format in the catalogue fits it, with an on-screen proof object and a show moment the growth evidence says holds people.
anchors.7: A catalogue format fits and there is one thing to show, not just say.
anchors.4: It can be made, but only as a talking head over stills.
anchors.1: A talking-head summary of an abstraction; nothing to show.

anchors.10: Clearly makes named people smarter, better, happier or more successful, at scale (config/good-news.json bar.helps).
anchors.7: Clearly helps a named group, at a modest scale.
anchors.4: Helps, but the people helped are vague.
anchors.1: Not good news for anyone in particular.

anchors.10: Reads as delight: a reader says out loud that they did not know that was possible.
anchors.7: A clear surprise in the facts.

anchors.10: Every story has a primary source from the actor itself or a peer-reviewed paper, dated inside the window.
anchors.7: Every story has a primary source; one is undated.
anchors.4: Some stories rest on a secondary report.

anchors.10: A reader in the sectors can do the thing today, with steps checked on the vendor's own documents.
anchors.7: Usable this week with one sign-up or setting.
anchors.4: Interesting but needs tools the reader does not have.

anchors.10: Three documented rungs, at least one a mechanism rung, explaining how it works in plain words.
anchors.7: One documented mechanism rung, clearly put.
anchors.4: The mechanism is asserted, not shown.

anchors.10: The actor's own domain or a filing, plus an independent second source.
anchors.7: The actor's own domain or a filing.
anchors.4: A reputable secondary report that links the primary.

anchors.10: Dated inside the edition week and first reported this week.
anchors.4: Last week, with a new development this week.

checks.probe_documented: Documented rungs from scripts/whys-probe-check.ts (quote verbatim in the cached page).
checks.landing_ok: The probe's landing is an open question with no landingVetoes (packages/contracts/src/whys.ts).
checks.primary_sources: Sources from the actor's own domain or a filing.
checks.sound_angle: At least one angle passed the soundness gate (angle.soundness).
checks.money_figure_sourced: A money figure (config/beat.json economics_keywords figure_pattern) quoted verbatim in the sourced fact.
checks.mechanism_rungs: Documented probe rungs with mechanism_type set.
checks.counter_rungs: Documented probe rungs whose counter is non-empty: a claim set against the evidence.
checks.comic_reading: The humour engine's comic_reading on the plain fact or the chosen line.
checks.needs_explaining: The humour engine needs more than one cultural or topical jump, or has missing context.
checks.template_ok: idea_checks.template_problems is empty and the captions pass the kill list.
checks.goodnews_checks: idea_checks.goodnews_findings finds nothing on the option.
checks.steps_verifiable: Every step is checked on the vendor's own documents.
checks.primary_source_own_domain: The primary source is the actor's own domain or a filing.

type_rules._about: Which type an option is scored as. First match wins.

rules.when: weekly good news, or a Saturday option

humour_map._about: The humour engine's labels as a 0-10 score (humour_check.py labels). An unread humour axis is null: it abstains, the option is marked humour unread, and it is never rank 1 on a short or meme day. An unavailable read is never a pass.

lenses.brief: the series lens: the money (Monday), how it works (Wednesday), the claim against the evidence (Friday)
the funniest true reading of the sourced facts, never a joke that costs credibility
the most absurd true detail in the sources

angle.humour_margin_note: On the 0-10 angle score: the funniest or most absurd true angle (comic_reading supported, mechanism in absurd_mechanisms) wins over the best angle only when sound and within this margin.

close.margin_note: Of 100: a slot's top two within this are a close call.
close.fork_note: Also close: both within 8 and one leads on absurdity_humour by 3 or more while the other leads on scale or whys by 3 or more.

council.barred_note: The ai-harness council's When it runs section admits Krish's ask or the strategist only, so until a ruling adds this caller a close call shows as close call, your pick, never a silent pass (commit 0 readiness).

unit_costs._about: Dollars reserved in the ledger before each call (.cache/story-score/spend.jsonl); the metered cost is recorded after. score_judge is the route's up-front estimate ($0.10) with headroom for up to 4 model calls at the model's price (commit 0 readiness, control-center api/_divergent.ts).

spend.note: Under the route's 20 quick ops and $5 a day, and the $15 weekly chain (config/chain-cap.json). The chain cap is checked first; over any cap the call is refused and the step is reported skipped, never passed.

growth_evidence._about: Performance data, not taste: what held people on the channels, read only from krishanraja/growth-makeyourmindup. Read by the fun_produce judge and the named_thing anchors.
